# Skill Set Configuration

This file is a template. The active config for each project lives at `.claude/plan-workflow-config.yml` in the project directory. Run `/configure-plan-plugin` to generate it.

## Config Format

### YAML (primary — generated by `/configure-plan-plugin`)

```yaml
# plan-workflow configuration
# Generated by /configure-plan-plugin. Run it again to update.

repo: <owner/repo>
project_number: <N>
project_id: <PVT_...>
status_field_id: <PVTSSF_...>
worktree_base: .worktrees

statuses:
  backlog: <option-id>
  ready: <option-id>
  in_progress: <option-id>
  in_review: <option-id>
  done: <option-id>

test_commands:
  backend: <command>
  frontend: <command or "none">
```

### Markdown table (legacy — still supported, no migration required)

Projects created before PLAN-00002 may have `.claude/plan-workflow-config.md` in the old
markdown table format. The `marvin` CLI reads both formats. If both files are present in the
same `.claude/` directory, YAML wins.

```markdown
# Skill Set Configuration

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| GitHub repo | `<owner/repo>` |
| Project number | `<N>` |
| Project ID | `<PVT_...>` |
| Status field ID | `<PVTSSF_...>` |
| Worktree base | `.worktrees` |
| "Backlog" option ID | `<option-id>` |
| "Ready" option ID | `<option-id>` |
| "In Progress" option ID | `<option-id>` |
| "In Review" option ID | `<option-id>` |
| "Done" option ID | `<option-id>` |
```

## Config Discovery and Precedence

`marvin config get <key>` discovers the config by walking up from the current directory,
checking `.claude/plan-workflow-config.yml` (YAML) first and `.claude/plan-workflow-config.md`
(legacy markdown) second. Skills call `marvin config get` rather than reading the file
directly; `marvin` handles format selection and field mapping transparently.

Precedence rules (highest to lowest):
1. `--config <path>` flag on any `marvin` invocation
2. `.claude/plan-workflow-config.yml` found by CWD-walk
3. `.claude/plan-workflow-config.md` found by CWD-walk (legacy fallback)

## Plan Template Resolution

Skills that render plan issue bodies resolve the template for each plan type using this order:

1. **Project override** (wins if present): `.claude/plan-workflow-templates/{type}.yml` in the consuming project — sibling to the config file.
2. **Plugin default** (always present): `skills/SHARED/templates/{type}.yml` in the plugin.

Where `{type}` is `arch-plan`, `impl-plan`, or `impl-phase`. A skill checks for the project override first; if the file is absent, it reads the plugin default. The plugin default is always present, so rendering never fails for lack of a template.

## Test Commands

Run from the **repository root**. Use the framework's native invocation pattern so commands start with the test runner binary and match any permission allowlists.

| Scope | Command (run from repo root) |
|---|---|
| Backend | *(configure for your project)* |
| Frontend | *(configure for your project)* |

## Board and Issue Operations

`marvin` (the bundled CLI, compiled into `${PLUGIN_DIR}/bin/marvin` by `deploy.sh`) handles
all board and issue read operations. Skills call `marvin board`, `marvin issue`, and related
subcommands rather than constructing raw `gh project` or `gh issue list` invocations.

### Reading board state

```bash
# All items currently on the board — plain text, one line per item:
# <number> | <status> | <title>
marvin board list

# Items filtered by status — accepts any form: "in_progress", "in-progress", "In Progress"
marvin board list --status in_progress
marvin board list --status in_review

# Current board column for a specific issue ("not-on-board" if absent; always exits 0)
marvin board status <issue-number>
```

`--json` is available as an opt-in escape hatch and reproduces the old shape (a JSON array of `{number, title, status, url}`), e.g. `marvin board list --json`.

### Listing issues

```bash
# All open issues with a given label — plain text, one line per issue:
# <number> | <state> | <labels-comma-joined> | <title>
marvin issue list --label "plan:phase"
```

To find every issue belonging to a specific plan (arch, impl, or phase), prefer the hierarchy walk over title-prefix filtering:

```bash
marvin issue tree <impl-plan-issue-number>
```

This returns one pipe-delimited line per node — `<kind> | #<number> | <state> | <status> | <title>` — with `kind` one of `arch`, `impl`, `phase`. Filter for lines where `kind` is `phase`. If zero `phase` lines are found (not the same as an empty result — `issue tree` always emits the target's own node), the plan predates sub-issue linking; fall back to:

```bash
marvin issue list --label "plan:phase" --title-prefix "[PLAN-XXXXX-" --state all
```

Note the trailing hyphen and **no closing bracket** — this is a true string-prefix match against phase titles like `[PLAN-XXXXX-1] ...`, unlike the closing-bracket form. For a multi-impl track (`[PLAN-XXXXX-A]`, `[PLAN-XXXXX-B]` — see `GLOSSARY.md`), apply the same rule one level deeper and use `--title-prefix "[PLAN-XXXXX-<suffix>-"` (e.g. `"[PLAN-00042-A-"`), so the fallback does not also match the sibling track's phases.

```bash
# Check phase completion via --json for jq post-processing: items with state != "CLOSED" are not done
marvin issue list --label "plan:phase" --title-prefix "[PLAN-XXXXX-" --state all --json \
  | jq '[.[] | select(.state != "CLOSED")]'
```

`marvin issue list` always exits 0. It outputs plain text by default (empty output when no results); pass `--json` for a JSON array (empty array `[]` when no results).

### Moving issues on the board

```bash
# Add issue to board, set status, and sync GitHub open/closed state
marvin board move <issue-number> <status>
```

### Raw API reference (for debugging outside skills)

These raw `gh` calls are what `marvin board` wraps. Use them only when debugging or scripting
directly outside a skill context.

```bash
# Add an issue to the board — use --jq to avoid piping through shell jq
ITEM_ID=$(gh project item-add <project-number> --owner <owner> \
  --url https://github.com/<repo>/issues/<issue-number> \
  --format json --jq '.id')

# Set the status field on a board item
gh project item-edit --id <item-id> \
  --project-id <project-id> \
  --field-id <status-field-id> \
  --single-select-option-id <option-id>
```
